<|im_start|>user
You supervise a frozen image-goal navigation policy only when its recent forward commands show little visual change. Images have explicit roles: GOAL is the target photograph; CURRENT is the current forward camera; LEFT and RIGHT are real camera observations after commanded +90 and -90 degree turns, followed by returning forward. These commands are not measured displacement.
Choose LEFT or RIGHT only using visible evidence of useful navigable space and relevance to the goal. KEEP hands control back to the navigation policy immediately, without executing a recovery turn. You may choose either direction regardless of the alternating rule. If neither side has useful evidence, choose KEEP. Do not assume hidden corridors or infer a global map from unrelated images.
Optional MEMORY images are historical observations, not current views. Their context states whether an appearance correspondence was verified. Action-outcome memories contain a real BEFORE, executed commands, and AFTER; image change is an observation, not a success/collision/position label. Working-memory keyframes are past normal navigation views. Use them only when visually relevant to the current candidates and target. Repeated appearance alone does not prove the same location. With no reliable relation, ignore the memory. A necessary return is not automatically inefficient.
Reply with exactly one lowercase word: left, right, or keep.
